stories.title: The Class Play
stories.text: On Thursday afternoon, Zara waited behind the red curtain in the school gym. She wore a crown made of gold paper. The class play would start in two minutes. Kofi peeked through a gap in the curtain. "The chairs are filling up," he whispered. Zara's knees began to shake. She had practiced her lines all week, but now her mind was empty. "Kofi, what do I say first?" she asked. Kofi did not know. He had never learned her part.
stories.problem: Zara cannot remember her first line.
far: Kofi trips over a cable and falls off the stage.
near: The play starts an hour late.
Kofi cannot find the costume he must wear.

stories.title: The Front Desk
stories.text: On a rainy Monday morning, Yusuf stood at the front desk of the school library. His library book about volcanoes was due today. He unzipped his backpack and looked inside. There was a lunch box, a pencil case, and a folder, but no book. "I put it in my bag last night," Yusuf said. Mrs. Novak, the librarian, smiled kindly. "Let's see what we can do," she said. Yusuf felt his face get hot.
stories.problem: Yusuf's library book is not in his backpack.
far: Yusuf spills paint on his folder.
Mrs. Novak cannot find her glasses anywhere today.
near: Yusuf's library book has a torn page.
Yusuf forgets his lunch box and his water bottle.
stories.topic: a library book left at home

stories.title: The Three-Legged Race
stories.text: On field day in June, Ines and Nico stood at the starting line on the school field. They tied Ines's left leg to Nico's right leg with a soft green scarf. "Ready?" asked Nico. They took one big step, and both of them fell flat on the grass. They got up and tried again. Down they went! "We keep falling," said Ines, rubbing her elbow. The three-legged race would begin in five minutes.
stories.problem: Ines and Nico keep falling when they walk.
far: Ines forgets her lunch and has nothing to eat.
near: The green scarf rips in half.
Nico hurts his elbow and has to see the nurse.

stories.title: Just Before the Bell
stories.text: Just before the bell on Thursday morning, Ravi and Grace carried the class bean plant down the hallway. The pot was heavy, and dirt spilled over the edge. They stopped at the science room. Ravi turned the doorknob, but the door did not open. He tried again. It was locked. "We need to put the plant by the window before class," said Grace. Her arms were starting to shake.
stories.problem: The door to the science room is locked.
far: Grace falls on the playground and hurts her knee.
near: Ravi drops the pot, and it breaks into pieces.
The science room is too dark.
stories.also: They cannot put the plant by the window before class.

stories.title: A Soft Thump
stories.text: At recess on Monday, Hugo and Nia ran out to the school field with the class soccer ball. Nia gave it a big kick. It made a soft thump and rolled only a few feet. Hugo picked it up and squeezed it. The ball was squishy, like a pillow. "It's flat!" he said. Nia looked in the ball bin by the door. The pump was not there. "We can't play like this," she said.
stories.problem: The soccer ball is flat.
far: It starts to rain, and recess is moved inside.
near: The ball bin is broken, and the balls fall out.

stories.title: Not One Bubble
stories.text: On the morning of the science fair, Diego and Aisha set their clay volcano on a table in the science room. It was brown and green, with a little cup hidden at the top. Aisha poured in the baking soda. Diego poured in the vinegar. Nothing happened. No foam came up. Not one bubble! "It worked yesterday," said Diego. The fair would open in ten minutes.
stories.time: on the morning of the fair
stories.problem: Their volcano will not fizz.
far: Aisha leaves her poster for the fair at home.
near: They spill the vinegar on the floor.
stories.topic: a volcano that will not fizz

stories.title: Art Table Trouble
stories.text: On Wednesday afternoon, Lucy and Marcus sat at the art table in their classroom. They were making bee puppets on craft sticks. Marcus cut out a yellow paper bee. Lucy pulled the cap off the glue stick and rubbed it on a craft stick. Nothing stuck. The glue was dry and hard. "This is the last glue stick," said Lucy. Marcus held up the paper bee and sighed.
stories.problem: Their last glue stick is dried out.
far: Lucy is late because her school bus broke down.
near: They run out of yellow paper.
The craft stick snaps when Marcus picks it up.

stories.title: Getting Ready for Recess
stories.text: On a cold Tuesday morning, Nina and Owen got ready for recess by the coat hooks in the hallway. Nina pulled on her puffy purple coat. She tugged the zipper up, but it stopped halfway. It would not go up, and it would not go down. "It's stuck!" she said. Owen tried to pull it too. Outside, snow was falling, and the wind was howling. Nina could not go out with her coat open.
stories.problem: The zipper of Nina's coat is stuck.
far: Nina trips on the stairs and drops her books.
near: Owen's zipper is stuck, so he cannot zip his coat.

stories.title: The City at Night
stories.text: On Friday after lunch, Talia and Mr. Kim worked on the giant floor puzzle in the classroom. It showed a city with lights in every window. For a whole week, they had put it together piece by piece. Now only one hole was left, right in the middle of the moon. Talia looked in the box. It was empty. "Where is the last piece?" she asked. Mr. Kim shook his head.
stories.problem: The last piece of the puzzle is missing.
far: Mr. Kim loses his keys and cannot open the door.
near: The puzzle box is broken, and its lid is lost.

stories.title: Two Minutes Left
stories.text: On Wednesday morning, Kenji sat on the bench outside the gym. Gym class was about to start, and he had to change his shoes. But his shoelace had a tight knot in it. Kenji pulled at the knot with his fingers. It only got tighter. Sofia sat down next to him. "Gym starts in two minutes," she said. Kenji tugged harder, but the knot did not move.
stories.problem: Kenji's shoelace has a tight knot.
far: Kenji forgets his lunch and his water bottle.
near: Sofia's shoelace has a knot she cannot untie.

stories.title: Knots and Loops
stories.text: On a windy Thursday at recess, June and Felix pulled the long jump rope out of the bin on the blacktop. The rope was one big tangle of knots and loops. "Who put it away like this?" asked Felix. June found one end and pulled. The knots only got tighter. The jump-rope contest was after recess, and they had not practiced once.
stories.time: at recess on a windy Thursday
stories.problem: The jump rope is one big tangle.
far: June loses her hat somewhere on the way to school.
near: The jump rope is too short.
stories.also: They cannot practice for the contest.

stories.title: Say Cheese!
stories.text: It was picture day, and Andre and Lucia stood in line outside the library on Tuesday morning. Lucia looked at Andre and pointed. "There's a cowlick sticking up," she said. Andre touched the top of his head. A big tuft of hair stood up like a feather. He patted it down, but it popped right back up. The camera flashed inside the library. Andre was next in line.
stories.problem: Andre's hair is sticking up on picture day.
far: Andre forgets his backpack on the school bus.
near: Lucia's hair sticks straight up, and she is next.

stories.title: The New Song
stories.text: On Monday afternoon, Amara and Luca took their seats in the music room. Today they would play their song for the first time. Luca opened his case and took out his recorder. Amara opened her case too. It was empty! "My recorder is gone," Amara whispered. Luca looked under her chair. There was nothing there but a crayon. The music was about to begin.
stories.problem: Amara's recorder is not in its case.
far: Amara cannot find the lunchroom at lunchtime.
near: Amara's recorder is broken and only squeaks.

stories.title: Over the Bushes
stories.text: On a windy Saturday afternoon, Malik and his grandpa walked into Cedar Park with a paper trail map. They wanted to find the waterfall. His grandpa unfolded the map to look at it. Just then, a gust of wind snatched it out of his hands. The map flew over the bushes and landed in the creek. "Oh no!" said Malik. Now they did not know which trail led to the waterfall.
stories.problem: The wind blows their map into the creek.
far: His grandpa slips and falls into the cold creek.
near: Malik drops his water bottle on the long trail.
stories.also: They do not know which trail goes to the waterfall.

stories.title: Spelling Test Day
stories.text: On Wednesday morning, Hazel and Marco sat at their desks in the classroom. The spelling test would start in five minutes. Hazel picked up her pencil. The tip was dull and flat. Marco's pencil was dull too. They walked to the pencil sharpener by the window. Marco pushed his pencil in, but the sharpener did not buzz. "It's broken," said Hazel.
stories.problem: The pencil sharpener is broken.
far: Hazel spills her water all over the spelling test.
near: The spelling test is canceled because of snow.
stories.also: Their pencils are dull, and the sharpener is broken.

stories.title: Room 12
stories.text: On the first morning of third grade, I walked into the school with my friend Theo. I looked at the paper in my hand. It said Room 12. But the hallway only went up to Room 10! "Mia, where is your room?" asked Theo. "I don't know," I said. Theo waved and ran into Room 8. The bell began to ring, and I was still standing in the hallway.
stories.time: on the first morning of third grade
stories.problem: Mia cannot find her classroom.
far: Mia falls on the stairs on her way into school.
stories.topic: a classroom that cannot be found

stories.title: The Great White Shark
stories.text: After lunch on Friday, my friend Ben and I sat in the reading corner with a library book about sharks. Ben turned the page too fast. Rrrip! A long tear ran down the middle of the page, right through a great white shark. "Kai, look what I did," Ben whispered. I stared at the torn shark. The book had to go back to the library on Monday.
stories.problem: A page of the library book is torn.
far: Kai is late for school and misses reading time.
near: Ben spills a cup of water on the library book.

stories.title: The Puddle
stories.text: On a rainy Tuesday morning, I hurried up the front steps of the school. A big puddle sat on the top step. I jumped over it, but I did not jump far enough. Splash! My left shoe and sock were soaked. "Elena, your shoe!" said my friend Amir. Water squished between my toes with every step, and the school day had not even started.
stories.problem: Elena's shoe and sock are soaking wet.
far: Elena forgets her lunch and her book at home.
near: Elena's shoe has a hole, and her toe sticks out.

stories.title: Hic! Hic!
stories.text: On Thursday morning, our classroom was quiet for the spelling test. I wrote the first word. Then it started. Hic! I put my hand over my mouth. Hic! Hic! "Adam, hold your breath," whispered my friend Sara. I held my breath and counted to ten. It did not help. Hic! The next word was "giraffe," and I could not even hear it.
stories.problem: Adam cannot stop his hiccups during the test.
far: Adam falls off his chair and knocks over his desk.
near: The spelling words are much too hard for Adam.

stories.title: Like an Oven
stories.text: On a hot afternoon in June, our classroom felt like an oven. Jonah and I went to open the big window. I pushed up on the frame. It did not move. "Ava, push harder!" said Jonah. We both pushed until our arms hurt. The window was stuck tight. Outside, the leaves on the trees did not move at all, and the air was hot and still.
stories.time: on a hot afternoon in June
stories.problem: The classroom window is stuck.
far: Ava spills her paint all over the classroom floor.
near: The classroom door is stuck, and no one gets in.

stories.title: Stripes on the Wings
stories.text: At recess on Friday, my friend Nora and I made paper airplanes on the blacktop. Mine had red stripes on the wings. I threw it as hard as I could. It sailed up, up, up and landed on the roof of the school! "Luis, it's stuck up there," Nora said. I stared at the roof. That airplane took me all of recess to make, and the bell was about to ring.
stories.problem: Luis's paper airplane is stuck on the roof.
far: Luis loses his red jacket on the bus ride home.
near: The paper airplane rips in two.
Nora's paper airplane is stuck up in a tall tree.

stories.title: Hurry Up!
stories.text: On Tuesday morning, I sat on the bench by the gym door with only one sneaker on. My left sneaker was gone. I looked under the bench and behind the door. "Dev, hurry up!" called my friend Grace from the hallway. "I can't find my other shoe!" I called back. I could hear whistles and bouncing balls. Gym class had already started without me.
stories.problem: Dev cannot find his left sneaker.
far: Dev forgets his lunch on the day of a field trip.
near: Dev cannot find his gym shirt.
Grace's sneaker has a broken lace that won't tie.

stories.title: The Ride Home
stories.text: After school on Monday, I climbed onto Bus 9 and sat by the window. The bus turned left at the corner. My bus always turns right! I did not know these streets at all. "Ruby, this isn't your bus," said the girl next to me. It was Jada from my class. My stomach dropped. The bus kept rolling farther and farther away from my street.
stories.problem: Ruby is on the wrong bus.
far: Ruby forgets her homework at school on Friday.
near: The bus has a flat tire.
Jada is on the wrong bus by mistake today.

stories.title: Whoosh!
stories.text: On a sunny Saturday at the beach, my friend Eli and I built a sandcastle with four towers while my mom read nearby. We dug a moat all around it. Then a big wave rushed up the sand. Whoosh! It knocked down two towers and filled the moat with water. "Sam, the waves are coming closer!" Eli shouted. I looked at the ocean. The next wave was even bigger.
stories.problem: The waves are knocking down their sandcastle.
far: Sam gets a bad sunburn on his nose and his arms.
near: A big dog runs right through their sandcastle.

stories.title: Snap!
stories.text: On Wednesday morning, I sat at the long table in the art room with my friend Priya. We were making necklaces with clay beads. I tied a knot at the end of my string and held it up. Snap! The string broke, and beads bounced all over the floor. Some rolled under the shelves. "Zoe, your beads!" Priya cried. Art class would end in ten minutes, and my string was empty.
stories.problem: Zoe's string breaks, and her beads roll away.
far: Zoe forgets her coat and hat on the school bus.
near: Zoe's beads are the wrong color.
Priya's string is much too short to tie a knot.

orderStories.title: The Class Mural
events: One Monday morning, Ms. Reyes told the class they would paint a mural.
At lunch, Tomas and Kim drew ideas on a big sheet of paper.
After lunch, the class voted for a picture of the ocean.
Later that afternoon, everyone painted the blue water.
The next morning, they added fish and an orange crab.
Finally, they signed their names in the corner.
orderStories.first: the class hears about the mural

orderStories.title: The Birdhouse
events: On Monday, Felix and his grandpa drew a plan for a birdhouse.
On Tuesday, they cut the wood into six pieces.
On Wednesday, they nailed the pieces together.
On Thursday, Felix painted the birdhouse green.
On Friday, they hung it from a branch of the maple tree.
Finally, a little brown bird moved in.
orderStories.first: they draw the plan before they build

orderStories.title: The Big Storm
events: One morning, dark clouds rolled over the town.
At noon, the wind began to blow hard.
Later that afternoon, rain poured down the windows.
That evening, thunder boomed over the houses.
That night, Nate fell asleep to the sound of the rain.
The next morning, the sun came out over the puddles.
orderStories.first: the clouds come before the wind and rain

orderStories.title: Ruby and the Space Books
events: One Saturday morning, Ruby walked to the library with her aunt.
At noon, she checked out three books about space.
After lunch, she read the first book on a park bench.
Later that afternoon, she drew a rocket ship.
That night, she looked for the moon from her window.
The next morning, she wrote a story about a trip to the moon.
orderStories.first: she walks to the library before she reads the books

orderStories.title: The Apple Tree
events: In the fall, red apples hung from the old tree in the schoolyard.
In the winter, snow covered its bare branches.
In the spring, white flowers opened on every twig.
In the summer, tiny green apples began to grow.
The next fall, the class picked a big basket of red apples.
Finally, they made applesauce in the classroom.
orderStories.first: the red apples of the first fall; The next fall closes the circle
orderStories.topic: an apple tree through the year

orderStories.title: Rusty's First Week
events: On Monday, the Lopez family brought home a puppy named Rusty.
On Tuesday, Rusty chewed up a sock.
On Wednesday, he learned to sit.
On Thursday, he walked on a leash for the first time.
On Friday, he slept all night in his own bed.
On Saturday, he played fetch in the park.
orderStories.first: the family brings the puppy home

orderStories.title: The Dinosaur Museum
events: Early one morning, Class 3B climbed onto a yellow bus.
At noon, they ate lunch on the grass by the museum.
After lunch, they saw a giant dinosaur skeleton.
Later that afternoon, they rode the bus back to school.
That evening, Lena told her family about the dinosaur.
That night, she dreamed that a dinosaur came to her school.
orderStories.first: the class gets on the bus

orderStories.title: Do Plants Need Light?
events: On Monday, Oscar asked a question: Do plants need light?
On Tuesday, he put one plant in a dark closet and one by a window.
On Wednesday, the plant by the window had a new leaf.
On Thursday, the plant in the closet looked pale and weak.
On Friday, he wrote down what he saw.
Finally, he shared his answer with the class.
orderStories.first: he asks the question before he tests it

orderStories.title: The Backyard Campout
events: One Saturday morning, Maya and her dad set up a tent in the yard.
At noon, they gathered sticks for a small fire.
Later that afternoon, they hung a lantern inside the tent.
That evening, they cooked corn over the fire.
That night, they counted stars through the tent door.
The next morning, they woke up to birds singing.

orderStories.title: Zoe Learns to Ride
events: On Monday, Zoe put on her helmet, tried to ride, and fell right away.
On Tuesday, she rode a few feet before she tipped over.
On Wednesday, she rode to the end of the sidewalk.
On Thursday, she rode around the block with her dad.
On Friday, she rode without a single wobble.
On Saturday, she rode all the way to the park with her dad.
orderStories.first: she falls on the first try

orderStories.title: The Spelling Bee
events: Before school, Ari practiced his spelling words one more time.
At lunch, he quizzed himself while he ate.
After lunch, the spelling bee began in the gym.
Later that afternoon, only Ari and one other girl were left.
That evening, he told his family that he came in second.
That night, he put his ribbon next to his bed.
orderStories.first: he practices before the spelling bee

orderStories.title: The Chicks Hatch
events: On Monday, a tiny crack appeared on one of the eggs.
On Tuesday, a little beak poked through the shell.
On Wednesday, a wet, fluffy chick wiggled out.
On Thursday, the chick was dry and yellow.
On Friday, two more chicks hatched.
Finally, the class took the chicks to a farm.
orderStories.first: a crack appears before a chick comes out

orderStories.title: The Puppet Show
events: On Monday, Maya and Tariq wrote a puppet show about a brave frog.
On Tuesday, they made puppets out of paper bags.
On Wednesday, they painted a pond on a big box.
On Thursday, they practiced the show three times.
On Friday, they put on the show for the first graders.
Finally, the first graders asked to see it again.
orderStories.first: they write the show before they make puppets

orderStories.title: Clean-Up Day
events: One Saturday morning, Ana's class met at the park to pick up trash.
At noon, they ate lunch under a big oak tree.
After lunch, they planted three small bushes.
Later that afternoon, they painted the old bench green.
That evening, Ana told her family about the park.
The next morning, she walked back to see the clean park.
orderStories.first: the class meets at the park

orderStories.title: The Kitten at the Door
events: Early one morning, a small gray kitten sat by the school door.
At noon, the principal gave it a bowl of water.
After lunch, the class made a sign about the lost kitten.
Later that afternoon, a girl ran up and said the kitten was hers.
That evening, the kitten slept on her bed.
The next morning, the girl brought the class a thank-you card.
orderStories.first: the kitten is found at the door
